source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Social anxiety disorder, in which the core fear is scrutiny or embarrassment rather than contamination obsessions with washing rituals.","B":"Body dysmorphic disorder, in which the central preoccupation is perceived appearance defects rather than contamination fears.","C":"Obsessive-compulsive disorder, in which intrusive contamination obsessions can drive time-consuming cleaning or handwashing compulsions.","D":"Generalized anxiety disorder, in which broad excessive worry occurs without repetitive compulsions performed in response to obsessions."}}
source_row.rationale: NIMH describes OCD as involving obsessions and compulsions; excessive cleaning or handwashing is a common compulsion, and clinically significant symptoms are time-consuming or cause distress/interference.

source_row.stem: A client spends several hours each day performing repetitive handwashing rituals in response to intrusive contamination fears and has marked distress when unable to complete them. Which condition is most consistent with this pattern?
